Sei que muita gente considera esse um dos melhores filmes de suspense já feitos, mas simplesmente não funcionou comigo. Tentei assistir mais de uma vez e nunca consegui terminar. Acho o ritmo muito lento, a história demora demais e o filme não consegue prender minha atenção. Todo mundo fala que o final é absurdo, mas eu nunca consegui chegar até ele porque sempre acabo perdendo o interesse no meio do caminho, acabei procurando pelo spoiler.

Another one for psych class. This is one of the worst films I've ever seen. The performances are mediocre, with DiCaprio's likely being the worst. The writing is incredibly juvenile, even with the plausible theory that the majority of the dialogue is filtered through the guy's warped mind. The film doesn't even look good or have an interesting aesthetic. The twist falls apart because it requires you to empathize with DiCaprio's character in the beginning, which I did not. Now, to the big problems. This film's portrayal of the mentally ill is disgusting. I understand that the facility is specifically meant to house people who've committed a violent crime, but the film was arguably still irresponsible in its perpetuation of the stereotype that all people with mental illness are scary, violent, completely irrational, and are deserving of no empathy whatsoever. There is no mention of the specific diagnosis that any patient, let alone the main character, has, which makes it impossible to understand the accuracy of the portrayals. This film was made too recently to still exhibit such an under-researched and outdated parody of what a real group of underprivileged people is like. Let's move on to another problem, the film's portrayal of both the Holocaust and the implications of Project MKUltra during the Cold War. These were both serious tragedies that I feel were not handled with appropriate sensitivity and were rather just half-baked elements seemingly thrown in for added novelty. With this film exhibiting these two themes in addition to its portrayal of extreme psychosis, there are too many things being explored and none of them are done properly. The main conspiracy is clearly supposed to be MKUltra, something that really did victimize psychiatric patients during the Cold War, and yet in the movie's cannon, it's confirmed to not be happening. I don't think this film is intentionally trying to say that MKUltra didn't happen, but it's a very strange and poorly thought-out choice that is completely at odds with the setting. This movie clearly did not have anything to say about any of the incredibly serious topics it includes, and thus has no comprehensive or unique thesis. It's an offensive, confused mess that frankly has no merit as a piece of art.

Non avendo mai avuto una particolare affinità con i film di Scorsese, partivo già con aspettative piuttosto basse e, purtroppo, sono state confermate. Il famoso plot twist, che tutti definiscono incredibile, a me non ha colpito per niente, più che sorprendermi mi ha lasciata completamente confusa. Anche dopo la fine del film continuo a pensare che la versione iniziale della storia abbia più senso di quella reale, pur sapendo che non è quella corretta. Probabilmente è uno di quei film che richiedono una seconda visione, ma personalmente non mi ha coinvolta abbastanza da volerlo rivedere. Ho apprezzato l’atmosfera inquietante e la fotografia, ma la narrazione mi è sembrata troppo contorta e il finale, invece di lasciarmi a bocca aperta, mi ha lasciata solo con la sensazione di non averci capito molto. Capisco perché sia considerato un cult, ma per me non ha funzionato

Pretty great idea but many many flaws. The twist is explained with a monologue and a whiteboard. The pacing drags in the middle section. It doesn’t drive the movie forward and the majority of it doesnt actually contribute to the narrative. Scorcese didn’t have a thought about the outside world in his mind while making the movie. I don’t need heavy social commentary, but at least a little something about the world. Not this one though. Scorcese doesnt seem to care about the mystery itself. He drops unbelievably obvious clues and it just makes the reveal even more of a letdown. So it’s a cool concept (with a whole lot of potential) with genuinely horrible execution. I kinda like the Fire and Water symbolism i guess and the setting is cool. And I love to see those main two actors doing their thing. But I can’t give I movie that’s js so bad in so many ways more than a 2

A bit confusing what about this script Scorsese and DiCaprio found compelling. It’s remarkably dry as a “suspense” film outside of a moody opening 15 minutes or so. It doesn’t have exciting moments scene to scene but rather a lot of chatter about the central “mystery”, but of course when the rug is pulled by the ending, all that is rendered mostly moot. And so at best you’re left with a Sixth Sense opportunity to rewatch the movie to see if you can spot the clues and even those aren’t particularly exciting to revisit.

In that big Scorsese bio doc that came out last year, DiCaprio said that Scorsese wasn't his usual self while directing Shutter Island, making it seem like the darkness of the material was getting to him. I feel like I can tell that he was in a bad place while watching this. I appreciate the usual Scorsese stuff like performances and shot compositions, but the vibe is so crushingly bleak and the subject is so dark that I had a hard time sitting through it today. I remember really enjoying it in the past, so maybe I'm just not in the right headspace for something like this right now. On the plus side, this watch helped my progress in two of my 2026 projects: Scorsese Summer and the year of WWII

"You have to let her go" "I can't!" "Then you'll never get off this island..." Enjoyed this more on rewatch, I was better able to appreciate how the mood of the island is developed, with the soundscape being particularly impressive, with original score, licensed music, and classical music all coming together really well. Weather is also used particularly effectively to make the island feel isolating and uncomfortable; there's something about heavy rain at night that makes me really uncomfortable and I love the way that is used in this film. The star segment here is Ward C, feeling like walking into a nightmare within an already dreadful environment - it feels like those segments in Silent Hill when you go from normal world to Otherworld, everything just gets so suddenly worse and terrifying with no end in sight. Despite this being a psychological thriller with heavy emphasis on its ending, it still does very little for me compared to the build up on the island (which I really enjoyed) and other films in the ending-heavy "genre" (Memento, Prestige, Fight Club, Total Recall, etc.). It just never feels like the reveals that happen meaningfully impact or re-contextualize the earlier scenes of the film. Of course the context does literally change but it doesn't really change the emotional impacts, at least for me

So why do you think Shutter Island hasn’t aged as well as his other works? Even Scorsese himself said he regrets being attached to it, and I think that’s wrong because it shows just how versatile the guy is. He can direct any genre to perfection.

Absolutely fantastic. Shutter Island is the kind of movie that gets better the more you think about it. The atmosphere is incredibly dark and unsettling, and Scorsese does an amazing job slowly building this feeling that something is seriously wrong without giving everything away. Leonardo DiCaprio is phenomenal here, carrying the entire movie with a performance that feels increasingly desperate and unhinged as the story progresses. The mystery constantly keeps you questioning what’s real and what isn’t, and the ending completely changes the way you look at everything that came before it. The cinematography, score, performances, and psychological tension all come together perfectly. It’s one of those movies where you immediately want to go back and watch it again just to catch everything you missed the first time. Fantastic
